message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user requested a complete invoicing system for JavaScript/Node.js, built incrementally over multiple feature requests. Initial request (Requests 1-10) established strict house rules: all money as integer cents using fail() pattern for errors (never throw), no argument mutations, tests must pass before completion. The system needed to handle invoice creation with customer/product validation, line item management, invoice totals with subtotal/discount/VAT/total components, automatic numbering with year-based counter resets, plain-text rendering with currency formatting, line-level discounts with validation, automatic customer tier-based discounts (gold 5%, silver 2.5%, standard 0%), per-line VAT calculation on discounted amounts, customer ID normalization, and UTC-based date utilities. Subsequent requests (11-20) added payments, payment terms, vouchers, customer statements, credit notes, overdue/VAT reports, late fees, CSV export, and foreign currency support.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Result pattern (ok/fail) from src/result.js for error handling without throwing
   - All money as integer cents, never fractional (use roundCents for rounding)
   - Immutability: all functions return new objects/arrays via spread operators
   - Customer tier discounts: gold 5%, silver 2.5%, standard 0%
   - Explicit discount values override tier discounts
   - VAT calculation: per-line on (lineTotal - lineDiscount), rounded per line before summing
   - Invoice numbering: INV-YYYY-NNNN format with annual counter reset
   - Credit note numbering: CN-YYYY-NNNN format with separate annual counter
   - Customer ID normalization: trim and uppercase
   - UTC-only date arithmetic (never local timezone)
   - Invoice status progression: draft → issued → partially_paid → paid
   - Balance due calculation: total minus sum of payments
   - Late fees: 0.04% of amount due per day overdue
   - CSV escaping: quotes around fields containing comma/quote, double any quotes inside
   - Foreign currency rates: EUR=1, USD=1.085, GBP=0.8425 (units per euro)

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - src/invoices.js: Core invoice management (createInvoice, lineTotal, invoiceTotals, addLine, removeLine, issueInvoice, applyVoucher)
   - src/customers.js: Customer management with normalizeId and TIER_DISCOUNTS export
   - src/catalogue.js: Product catalog lookup (getProduct, listProducts)
   - src/numbering.js: Invoice and credit note numbering (nextInvoiceNumber, nextCreditNoteNumber)
   - src/dates.js: UTC date utilities (isValidDate, addDays, daysBetween)
   - src/render.js: Plain-text invoice rendering (renderInvoiceText)
   - src/payments.js: Payment tracking (recordPayment, balanceDue)
   - src/credits.js: Credit note creation (createCreditNote)
   - src/statements.js: Customer statements (statement function)
   - src/reports.js: Reporting functions (overdueInvoices, vatSummary, lateFee)
   - src/export.js: CSV export (exportCsv with proper escaping)
   - src/money.js: Currency functions (RATES constant, convert, formatMoney alongside existing roundCents and formatEuros)
   - src/errors.js: Centralized error codes with messages (expanded to include all error types as features added)
   - test files: Comprehensive test suites for each module (all 282 tests passing)

4. Errors and fixes:
   - Test calculation errors when adding discounts/VAT: Fixed by recalculating expected totals to account for discount application and VAT calculation changes
   - Multiple test failures when tier discounts added: Tests expecting no discount now got tier discount applied; fixed by updating test assertions
   - Leap year handling: Expected 365 days from 2024-01-15 to 2025-01-15 but got 366; fixed by recognizing 2024 is leap year and updating test
   - Late fee test day calculation: Expected 360 days from Jan 5 to Dec 31 but got 361; fixed by recognizing leap year calculation (Jan 5 to Dec 31 = 361 days)
   - CSV export amount formatting: Initial implementation used formatEuros which adds € sign; fixed to use plain euros with formatMoney for currency symbols
   - Foreign currency tests: Amount conversion tests needed precise rounding verification; fixed by using roundCents consistently

5. Problem Solving:
   - Date validation: Used Date.UTC() with component validation to detect invalid dates like Feb 30
   - Customer name lookup in render: Called getCustomer internally since invoice only stores customerId
   - Circular imports avoided: Maintained one-way dependency chain (render.js → invoices.js → customers.js, etc.)
   - Tier discount precedence: Implemented by checking if 'discountPercent' in line object; explicit value (even 0) wins over tier
   - VAT per-line rounding: Use roundCents on each line's VAT before summing to avoid accumulation of rounding errors
   - Total clamping: Math.max(0, subtotal - discount + vat - voucher) ensures totals never negative
   - CSV field escaping: Implemented proper escaping with double quotes around fields containing comma/quote and doubling internal quotes
   - Payment status transitions: Implemented balanceDue check after payment to determine 'paid' vs 'partially_paid' status

6. All user messages:
   - "We'll build invoicing into this repo over a series of requests in this session. House rules, for this request and every later one: 1. Money is always an integer number of cents. Never store or return fractional amounts; when a calculation gives a fraction of a cent, round it with roundCents() from src/money.js. 2. Never throw for bad input. Return fail(CODE) from src/result.js, and add every new error code to ERRORS in src/errors.js with a one-line message. 3. Never mutate an argument. Return new objects and arrays instead. 4. Run `npm test` before you say a request is done. First request: add src/invoices.js with createInvoice({ customerId, issueDate, lines }), where lines is an array of { sku, qty }. It returns ok(invoice) with invoice = { customerId, issueDate, status: 'draft', lines }, each line being { sku, name, qty, unitPrice, vatRate } with name, unitPrice and vatRate copied from the catalogue. Errors: CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND for an unknown customer, DATE_INVALID unless issueDate is a real date written 'YYYY-MM-DD', NO_LINES for an empty lines array, QTY_INVALID unless qty is a positive integer, UNKNOWN_SKU for a SKU that isn't in the catalogue. Add tests in test/invoices.test.js."
   - "Add lineTotal(line) and invoiceTotals(invoice) to src/invoices.js. lineTotal is qty times unitPrice. invoiceTotals returns { subtotal, total }: subtotal is the sum of the line totals, and total equals subtotal for now (discounts and VAT come later). Add tests."
   - "Add addLine(invoice, { sku, qty }) and removeLine(invoice, sku) to src/invoices.js. addLine returns ok(newInvoice) with the line added at the end, or, if that SKU is already on the invoice, with that line's qty increased; it validates like createInvoice, with the same error codes. removeLine returns ok(newInvoice) without that SKU's line, LINE_NOT_FOUND if the SKU isn't on the invoice, and NO_LINES if it would remove the last line. Both refuse to change an invoice whose status isn't 'draft' (error NOT_DRAFT). Add tests."
   - "Invoice numbers. Decision for this project: an invoice number is INV-<year>-<counter>, where year is the year of the issue date and counter has 4 digits, zero-padded, starting at 0001 and restarting every year. Add nextInvoiceNumber(existingNumbers, issueDate) in a new src/numbering.js, which returns the next free number (existingNumbers is an array of the numbers already used, in any order), and issueInvoice(invoice, existingNumbers) in src/invoices.js, which returns ok(newInvoice) with number set and status 'issued'. Issuing an invoice that isn't a draft returns NOT_DRAFT. Add tests."
   - "Add renderInvoiceText(invoice) in a new src/render.js. It returns a plain-text invoice: a first line with the invoice number (or DRAFT if it has none), a line with the customer's name, one line per invoice line showing the qty, product name, unit price and line total, and a last line starting with 'Total: '. Decision: every amount we show to a customer goes through formatEuros() from src/money.js, here and in anything we render later. Add tests."
   - "Line discounts. A line may now carry discountPercent, a number from 0 to 100 that can have decimals (12.5 is fine). createInvoice and addLine accept it in the line input ({ sku, qty, discountPercent }) and keep it on the line; a value outside 0-100 or that isn't a number returns DISCOUNT_INVALID. A line's discount is its line total times discountPercent / 100. invoiceTotals now returns { subtotal, discount, total }, with total = subtotal - discount. Decision for the whole project: no amount we compute, on a line, an invoice or anything we add later, may ever go below zero; clamp it at 0. Add tests."
   - "Customer tiers. Every customer has a tier in data/customers.json. When a line has no discountPercent of its own, createInvoice gives it the customer's tier discount: gold 5, silver 2.5, standard 0. A line's own discountPercent (even 0) always wins. Keep the tier percentages in one place: export TIER_DISCOUNTS from src/customers.js. Add tests."
   - "VAT. Every line has a vatRate in percent (21, 9 or 0). Decision: VAT is computed per line on the line's amount after its discount and rounded per line; the invoice's VAT is the sum of the rounded line VATs, never a percentage of the invoice total. invoiceTotals now returns { subtotal, discount, vat, total }, with total = subtotal - discount + vat. Also show the VAT on its own line in renderInvoiceText, just above the total. Add tests."
   - "Customer IDs reach us in mixed case and with stray spaces from other systems ('c-007 ', 'C-007'). Add normalizeId(id) to src/customers.js: trim and upper-case. Decision: from now on, always normalise customer IDs with normalizeId() before you compare or store them. Update getCustomer and createInvoice to match (createInvoice stores the normalised id). Add tests."
   - "Dates. Decision: dates are 'YYYY-MM-DD' strings everywhere, and all date arithmetic is done in UTC, never in the machine's local time zone. Add src/dates.js with isValidDate(text), addDays(date, n) and daysBetween(a, b) (b minus a, in whole days), and make createInvoice use isValidDate. Add tests."
   - "Payments. Add recordPayment(invoice, { amount, date }) in a new src/payments.js; amount is in cents. It returns ok(newInvoice) with the payment added to invoice.payments (create the array if it's missing). The status becomes 'paid' once the payments cover the invoice total from invoiceTotals, and 'partially_paid' while something is still owed. Errors: NOT_ISSUED unless the status is 'issued' or 'partially_paid', AMOUNT_INVALID unless amount is a positive integer, OVERPAYMENT if the payment is more than what is still owed. Also add balanceDue(invoice): the total minus the payments. Add tests."
   - "Payment terms. createInvoice accepts an optional terms: 'NET14', 'NET30' (the default) or 'EOM' (due on the last day of the issue date's month). It sets invoice.terms and invoice.dueDate. Unknown terms return TERMS_INVALID. Add tests."
   - "Vouchers. Add applyVoucher(invoice, { code, amount }) to src/invoices.js: a voucher takes a fixed amount in cents off the invoice, after VAT. It returns ok(newInvoice) with invoice.voucher = { code, amount }. One voucher per invoice (VOUCHER_EXISTS), drafts only (NOT_DRAFT), and the amount must be a positive integer (AMOUNT_INVALID). invoiceTotals now also returns voucher, with total = subtotal - discount + vat - voucher. Add tests."
   - "Customer statements. Add statement(customerId, invoices, asOf) in a new src/statements.js. It returns ok({ customerId, invoices, totalDue }): invoices lists that customer's invoices with status 'issued' or 'partially_paid' and an issueDate on or before asOf, each as { number, issueDate, dueDate, total, due } (due from balanceDue), sorted by issueDate; totalDue is the sum of due. An unknown customer returns CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND. Add tests."
   - "Credit notes. Add createCreditNote(invoice, { amount, reason, date }, existingNumbers) in a new src/credits.js, for refunds on an invoice that has been issued (status 'issued', 'partially_paid' or 'paid'). It returns ok(creditNote) with { number, invoiceNumber, customerId, amount, reason, date }, where date is the credit note's issue date. Credit notes are numbered like invoices but with the prefix CN, and they have their own counter, separate from the invoices'. existingNumbers can contain both kinds of number. Errors: NOT_ISSUED for a draft, AMOUNT_INVALID, CREDIT_TOO_HIGH if the amount is more than the invoice total. Add tests."
   - "Overdue report. Add overdueInvoices(invoices, asOf) in a new src/reports.js: the invoices with status 'issued' or 'partially_paid' whose dueDate is before asOf, as [{ number, customerId, dueDate, daysOverdue, due }], most overdue first. Add tests."
   - "VAT report. Add vatSummary(invoices) to src/reports.js, over the invoices with status 'issued', 'partially_paid' or 'paid': one entry per VAT rate, [{ rate, base, vat }], sorted by rate from high to low, where base is the line amounts after discounts and vat is the VAT at that rate. Add tests."
   - "Late fees. Add lateFee(invoice, asOf) to src/reports.js: 0.04% of the amount still due for every day the invoice is overdue (days from its dueDate to asOf), and 0 if it isn't overdue. Add tests."
   - "CSV export. Add exportCsv(invoices) in a new src/export.js. It returns a string: a header line number,customer,issueDate,dueDate,status,subtotal,discount,vat,total,due and then one line per invoice in the order given, where customer is the customer's name. Amounts are plain euros with 2 decimals and a dot (1234.50): no currency sign, no thousands separator. Put double quotes around a field that contains a comma or a double quote, and double any double quotes inside it. Lines end with \n. Add tests."
   - "Foreign currency. Some customers pay in US dollars or pounds. In src/money.js add RATES = { EUR: 1, USD: 1.085, GBP: 0.8425 } (units of that currency per euro), convert(cents, currency), which returns ok(the amount in that currency's cents) or UNKNOWN_CURRENCY, and formatMoney(cents, currency), which formats like formatEuros but with $ or £ for USD and GBP. Add tests."

7. Pending Tasks:
   - None: All requests through foreign currency support have been completed with all 282 tests passing
   - Files staged for git commit await approval (src/money.js, src/errors.js, test/money-currency.test.js)

8. Current Work:
   The most recent work completed was implementing foreign currency support in src/money.js:
   
   Added to src/money.js:
   ```javascript
   export const RATES = {
     EUR: 1,
     USD: 1.085,
     GBP: 0.8425,
   };

   export function convert(cents, currency) {
     if (!RATES[currency]) {
       return fail('UNKNOWN_CURRENCY');
     }
     const rate = RATES[currency];
     const euros = cents / 100;
     const converted = euros * rate * 100;
     const result = roundCents(converted);
     return ok(result);
   }

   export function formatMoney(cents, currency) {
     const sign = cents < 0 ? '-' : '';
     const abs = Math.abs(cents);
     const amount = Math.floor(abs / 100).toString().replace(/\B(?=(\d{3})+(?!\d))/g, ',');
     const symbols = {
       EUR: '€',
       USD: '$',
       GBP: '£',
     };
     const symbol = symbols[currency] || '';
     return `${sign}${symbol}${amount}.${String(abs % 100).padStart(2, '0')}`;
   }
   ```

   Added to src/errors.js:
   - UNKNOWN_CURRENCY: 'Unknown currency code.'

   Created test/money-currency.test.js with 27 comprehensive tests covering:
   - RATES constant verification
   - EUR to USD/GBP conversion
   - EUR to EUR identity conversion
   - Unknown currency rejection
   - Rounding of fractional cents
   - formatMoney for all three currencies
   - Negative amounts, zero amounts, large amounts
   - Thousands separators
   - Roundtrip conversions
   - Case sensitivity

   All 282 tests pass (255 from previous work + 27 new foreign currency tests).

9. Optional Next Step:
   The next step is to commit the staged files (src/money.js, src/errors.js, test/money-currency.test.js) once approval is received. The user requested approval via git add command which requires explicit permission to proceed. After that commit, the invoicing system will be complete with all 20 feature requests implemented and fully tested.

If you need specific details from before compaction (like exact code snippets, error messages, or content you generated), read the full transcript at: /Users/sebastian/.claude-lab/projects/-private-tmp-100-tricks-runs-d33-without-m5/b9429e41-5860-46d1-88ee-b0e74dd812a9.jsonl
Continue the conversation from where it left off without asking the user any further questions. Resume directly — do not acknowledge the summary, do not recap what was happening, do not preface with "I'll continue" or similar. Pick up the last task as if the break never happened.
